conventions.convention: Resolvents are (z-H) inverse; cluster contours are counterclockwise circles |z-E|=g/2. Complex couplings give Riesz idempotents; real couplings give orthogonal spectral projections. The finite-rank construction assumes Countable Choice and treats v=0 without dividing by v.
Inner products are linear in the first variable. Gauge normalization is ⟨ψ(λ),ψ0⟩=1, not unit norm; the holomorphic energy identity pairs the moving vector with the fixed second vector ψ0.

Trial vectors are unit vectors in Q(H)=D((H-cI)^(1/2)); trial values are the closed spectral form. Discrete eigenvalues start at E1, include multiplicity, and become Λ=inf essential spectrum after exhaustion; infimum of the empty set is +∞. The second min-max family uses dim F≤n−1.

W(ξ)=V(ℓξ)/E★, λ=E/E★, and h=ℏ/(ℓ√(2mE★)). The barrier action S is not divided by h; transmission has exponent −2S/h. Small-h limits keep W and λ fixed, with a corresponding physical family obtained by varying the width while keeping ℏ fixed.

The smooth barrier is C⁵ and compactly supported, with exactly two separated simple turning points. Exterior waves have reference currents ±1; T=|t|² is an exact scattering-current ratio, not a Born probability of a normalized preparation or a detector count.

For a positive-slope turning point, allowed-side phase is measured outward from the turn. The decaying branch has allowed amplitude 2C sin(θ+π/4), and the growing branch has C′ cos(θ+π/4). Oscillatory errors are additive, including at sine and cosine zeros.

The neutral pair has charges −q,+q and relative coordinate r=x1−x2, hence dipole D=−qr and interaction −Eext·D. Static Stark results use only finite-dimensional compressions on a subspace lying in the energy and coordinate domains; the uncompressed linear interaction is excluded.

load_bearing.statement: Under Countable Choice, a self-adjoint H0 with isolated eigenvalue E of finite rank r≥1 and gap g, perturbed by bounded self-adjoint V, has a holomorphic rank-r contour projection throughout 2|λ|‖V‖/g<1. Its finite restriction has exactly the enclosed spectrum; the complementary restriction has a bounded inverse at every point inside the circle. Real coupling gives the orthogonal cluster projection; V=0 is constant for all couplings.

Declares the effective spinless line model, a C⁵ compactly supported potential, the exact nondimensional equation u″=(W−λ)u/h², hypotheses W1–W3, the fixed-profile small-h family, and the unique boundary-defined scattering solution with T(h)=|t(h)|².

The C² equation u″=(W−λ)u/h² is equivalent under ψ(x)=u(x/ℓ) to −ℏ²ψ″/(2m)+E★W(x/ℓ)ψ=E★λψ. Under the respective strict-sign hypotheses, the dimensionless forbidden exponent and allowed phase equal their physical action integrals divided by ℏ.

For the declared WKB model with one simple positive-slope turning point, there are independent exact decaying and growing solutions with the stated Airy amplitude relations, additive allowed-side errors, relative forbidden-side errors, and value/derivative envelope estimates controlled by ε(h)=O(h) and h/|ζ|^(3/2) away from the turn.

For the declared simple gapped label and bounded perturbation with v>0, on |λ|<R=g/(8v), E′(0)=⟨Vψ0,ψ0⟩, ψ′(0)=−SVψ0, E″(0)=−2⟨VSVψ0,ψ0⟩, and the cubic remainder is at most Rv(|λ|/R)³/(1−|λ|/R). At |λ|=R/2 this is g/32. The v=0 family is constant without a divided radius.

Adopts the neutral Coulomb pair's compressed static dipole energy HS=ΠW Hκ|W−Σj Eext,j DjW on a declared finite-dimensional subspace in the energy and coordinate domains. The uncompressed nonzero-field interaction is unbounded, and its common-test-domain energy expectations tend to −∞ along the displayed translated test functions.

For the fixed C⁵ compactly supported barrier with exactly two separated simple turning points, |T(h)e^(2S/h)−1|≤C0[ε(h)+e^(−2S/h)]/[1−C0[ε(h)+e^(−2S/h)]] when the denominator is positive, with ε(h)≤C1h. In particular T(h)e^(2S/h)→1.

concerns.concern: Facts [F3] first defines η+=ζ(ξ0+s0), the fixed positive right endpoint, then writes φh(η)=2(η+)^(3/2)/(3h). The latter needs the positive part max(η,0), rather than the previously defined endpoint. The Statement and the cited Volterra supplier use the intended variable positive part, so this is a notation collision in the facts block.

The Teschl source description attributes 'one turning point and the transmission setup' to Section 9.7, printed pp. 214–220. The opened section instead gives relative bounds, essential/absolutely continuous spectra, large-x asymptotics in Lemma 9.37, Sturm comparison and oscillation criteria; it ends before Chapter 10 without an Airy turning-point connection or barrier-transmission setup. Correct the locator or limit the attribution. This does not replace or invalidate the separate local proof suppliers. Source checked: [Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics](https://www.mat.univie.ac.at/~gerald/ftp/book-schroe/schroe.pdf), Section 9.7.

The page says the two-level example 'reads off the second order coefficient −2c²/g'. The example correctly gives E″(0)=−2c²/g, while the coefficient of λ² in the Taylor expansion is −c²/g. Specify 'second derivative' or use the Taylor coefficient.

The orientation remark says 'Reversing the orientation of the interval would replace the sine by a cosine and vice versa.' This needs a precise phase convention: reversing the signed phase θ while retaining +π/4 produces that trigonometric rewrite, but reflecting the coordinate and retaining the declared nonnegative outward action does not exchange the decaying and growing connections. The barrier proof correctly uses coordinate reflection with outward phases. The standard Airy forms agree with the main Statement: [DLMF §9.7](https://dlmf.nist.gov/9.7), equations 9.7.9 and 9.7.11.
